newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Nov expiry lifts FTSE, OTM calls active.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Nov expiry lifts FTSE, OTM calls active.

text.p: The expiration of November index options on Friday helped push the FTSE 100 up toward the 3,950 level, the strike level that many were hoping to exercise, dealers said.
By 1307 GMT, the underlying index was up 28.0 points to 3,954.1, but narrowly missed the 3,950 mark on expiry this morning.
Turnover was heavy, fuelled by November expiry. Trading volume on the call side exceed volume on the put side, reversing the pattern seen this week.
But dealers said they didn't believe the increased activity in calls represented strategy trades or reflected a change in market sentiment.
"My guess is that the vast majority of these trades are hedge trades. I don't think anyone is taking a view on the market," said one.

Volume was particularly heavy in the American-style December 4100 calls, where almost 5,900 lots changed hands by 1307 GMT, and in December 4,000 calls, where 2,400 lots traded. In European-style options, more than December 4225 calls, where 6,100 lots were recorded.
Activity in Railtrack was active after the rail utility reported better-than-expected first-half results.
Railtrack shares jumped 35-1/2p to 320-1/2p, after having climbed as high as 324p, a record.
A flurry of options activity in Railtrack led up to today's results. Most of the deals this week were volatility trades, dealers said.
